doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Earliest music and improvising at the Steinway
summary: A Steinway was in the house from birth; he improvised from age two or three and his parents shielded him from formal study until seven.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Right. When you grew up in Chicago, can you recall the first — I know you came from a household that had a number of influences in it. What was the first music that made an impression on you?
My earliest? Like my earliest childhood—
The earliest that you can recall.

It must have been something at home because there was a Steinway piano in the house from the day I was born and before. And so I imagine what I first heard was one of my parents playing the piano or playing some 78 recording of some classical music. That’s

what I’m sure I heard first. My earliest experiences as a player was as an improviser. When I was about two or three years old, I still have dim memories of climbing up on the piano bench, often on the lap of whichever parent was playing, and I put my little hands on their hands and I would go along for the ride, kinesthetically, to get a sense of what it was like to traverse a keyboard. And then I would stay up there by myself and I would start playing stuff. And my folks gave me a tremendous gift by protecting me from formal study for a number of years. They sensed that I just needed time and space to just inhabit this musical world on my own terms and just improvise and make up things and do stuff. And then I guess when I was about seven years old I had a hunger at that point to formally study and that’s when I began to study the classical literature.
Yeah. They were very insightful then.
I think so. I think they did just the right thing for me.
Yeah. Because if they had, you know, if they had tried to make you one of those four- year-old little prodigies it might have stifled you.
